specification.title: A unique violation is caught inside the transaction, which then ends normally
steps: Start a transaction with the framework's ordinary transaction API.
Write the marker `tx`, and make sure the write was sent to PostgreSQL.
Checkpoint `after-write`: report pg_current_xact_id() and pg_backend_pid(), read through the transaction's own connection.

Insert the value 'taken' into uniq through the framework's ordinary write API. It fails with unique_violation (23505). Catch the error and continue. After catching the error, the callback sends nothing else and returns.
Checkpoint `before-end`: report the same backend PID. The transaction is aborted, so it cannot run queries; the runner confirms the aborted state server-side.
End the transaction normally, so that the framework sends COMMIT.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the API has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: When PostgreSQL has aborted the transaction before it ends, so that its COMMIT is answered with ROLLBACK, the API does not report a successful commit.

execution.description: Connection::beginTransaction(), Connection::commit(), and Connection::rollBack() on the same Capsule connection. A nested beginTransaction() is a savepoint. commit() at a level above 1 decrements Laravel's counter and does not send RELEASE SAVEPOINT. Eloquent creates write the markers. PDO::ATTR_PERSISTENT is false.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

fault.mechanism: A unique_violation raised by PostgreSQL inside the transaction, and caught by the application.
fault.injection_point: After the first write, before the transaction ends.
fault.preconditions: The row 'taken' already exists in uniq (fixture).
fault.expected_server: The failed statement aborts the transaction. PostgreSQL answers the later COMMIT with the command tag ROLLBACK, without an error, and commits nothing.
fault.expected_client: The driver receives the command tag ROLLBACK as the reply to COMMIT.

knowledge: The outcome reaches the client: PostgreSQL's reply to COMMIT carries the command tag ROLLBACK.

api_outcome.basis: Connection::commit() returned. At level 1 that calls PDO::commit() and does not inspect its return value or a command tag.
api_outcome.contract: Laravel 13.38.0 Connection::beginTransaction(), Connection::commit(), and Connection::rollBack() are the explicit API. The adapter calls beginTransaction(), runs the work, calls commit() when the work returns, and on a thrown error calls rollBack() and reports that error. commit() calls getPdo()->commit() only when transactionLevel() === 1, then decrements the counter and fires the committed event. It does not read a command tag. A nested beginTransaction() is SAVEPOINT transN. A nested rollBack() is ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT transN. A nested commit() does not send RELEASE SAVEPOINT. executeBeginTransactionStatement() does not take an isolation level. Session isolation, when requested, is PostgresConnector::configureIsolationLevel at connect time.

violation.message: SQLSTATE[23505]: Unique violation: 7 ERROR: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "uniq_code_key" DETAIL: Key (code)=(taken) already exists. (Connection: default, Host: 127.0.0.1, Port: 55435, Database: ppcs_tx_01a_caught_error_then_commit_mviboae7_9d7382, SQL: insert into "uniq" ("code") values (taken) returning "id")

select pg_current_xact_id()::text as xid, pg_backend_pid() as pid

evaluation.mechanism_detail: after the API returned, the session was "idle", and its last statement was "COMMIT"
evaluation.reason: TX-01A.1 violated: the API reported: committed

preconditions.description: the write of marker "tx" had reached PostgreSQL at `after-write` (a row lock on item, in pg_locks)
the duplicate insert failed with unique_violation (23505), as reported by the adapter
the top-level transaction was aborted before it ended: at `before-end` the session was "idle in transaction (aborted)" and pg_xact_status() already reported it aborted
PostgreSQL did not commit the transaction
